rationale: Evidence from iteration 0 (development simulator, no per-step telemetry): every trial on all three tracks ended off_track, with none finishing. Progress was 0.36 on the oval, 0.16 on the s-bend and 0.11 on the slalom. Each run logged exactly one line-loss event, and max_error reached about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 for any allowed body width). rms_error stayed small (0.03 m), so the robot tracks well until a single sharp moment throws it off the line and it never recovers. Steering oscillation was moderate (0.15-0.21), so the robot is not badly jittering. The likely cause is that at base_speed 1.6 the robot carries too much speed into the bends, and with kp 2.0 and kd 0.3 it under-corrects the error that builds up. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.6 -> 1.3, to slow entry into bends and cut the lateral error that causes the single loss; (2) kp 2.0 -> 3.0, for a firmer steer on sharper bends; (3) kd 0.3 -> 0.8, to damp the larger kp and keep oscillation under control. Geometry is kept as it was so this iteration isolates the controller change; body_width stays at 0.12 because the off-track limit is already at its 0.06 floor. Expected result: fewer off-track ends, the oval and s-bend progressing further, and possibly one finish on the oval. The finish time will be longer than 3 s at the lower speed, so the score may still be modest, but the progress and line-loss terms should rise. Hypotheses to check: (a) most failures come at one specific bend, and max_error occurs there; (b) the line loss happens at entry to the bend, so speed is the main factor; (c) if steering_oscillation rises with kd, kd is too high relative to kp. Next measurements: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort, to locate the failing bend and the loss timing.
